agent.problem: Acts 13:1 lists Manaen among the church's prophets and teachers but does not identify him specifically as a teacher. Calling him "one of the teachers" settles a distinction the verse leaves open; "one of the prophets and teachers" would stay with the text.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

agent.problem: The standalone question never identifies who "they" are. With the earlier Antioch setup no longer on screen, the people who fast, pray, lay on hands and send Barnabas and Saul off lack a clear antecedent.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

agent.problem: Too many choices depend on luck rather than reasoning from the earlier cards. There is no supplied basis for choosing John's role (card 10), Saul's other name (card 15), or Paul's announced consequence (card 17), while cards 2, 5 and 12 add further discovery-only picks. In an eleven-choice stop, this goes beyond a few discovery questions.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer. A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.
